sn47.19:1.1: This may be modern Sambalpur in Odisha, near the bay of Bengal on India’s east coast. 500km further east lies Chandraketugarh in West Bengal, where the earliest physical evidence for pole acrobatics or *mallakambha* has been found. One pot from around 200 BCE shows, in detailed and graceful style, three acrobats using a T-shaped pole. One man kneels, holding the pole with great strength and balance, while a man and a woman perform acrobatics on opposite bars of the T. A crowd of women and men look on in amazement.
sn47.19:1.3: This appears to be the oldest reference to pole dancing, knows as mallakambha https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallakhamba
sn47.19:1.4: Medakathālikā was female, as depicted on the Chandraketugarh pottery.
